title: Ordinary etale finite-type coordinate support orientation and field normalization
statement:
Fix the finite datum $k,\ell,E,n,A$ of [def-pur-conventions], with arbitrary $n\geq1$, and the twists of [def-coefficient-twists-detailed]. Let $B$ be an affine finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-finite-type-morphism], let $b\geq0$, and put $P=\mathbf A^b_B$ with zero section $z:B\hookrightarrow P$ [def-sbc-affine-space]. On the small etale site [def-weil-pbc-etale-site], use sheaves of $A$-modules and the support kernel $Q_z$ of [def-pur-etale-coordinate-support]: $Q_z(F)(W)=\ker(F(W)\to F(W\setminus (B\times_PW)))$. Write $RQ_z$ for its bounded-below right derived functor [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories]. For every integer $r$ there is a canonical isomorphism
$$RQ_z(A_P(r))\simeq z_*A_B(r-b)[-2b].$$
It is normalized so that, for $r=b$, the element $1$ on $B$ corresponds to the ordered supported Cartier-Kummer product $\partial\kappa(v_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(v_b)$; for $b=0$ this is the unit. Here each boundary is the ordinary etale boundary with coefficients $\mu_{\ell^N}\otimes_{\mathbf Z/\ell^N}A$ for any $N\geq1$ killing $A$, identified with the specified finite twist by [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map], and the product is [def-pur-supported-cup] read on its ordinary etale witness. For arbitrary $r$ the normalization is tensored with the constant rank-one line $L_{r-b}=A(r-b)(k)$, using [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback]. The isomorphisms are independent of a basis of that line and of $N$, commute with every base change between affine finite-type $k$-schemes through the canonical supported pullback maps, and respect $A(r)=A(b)\otimes_A A(r-b)$, including negative twists defined by dual powers.
The identification uses the ordinary closed-support right adjoint: if $z^!_0=z^{-1}Q_z$, then $Q_z=z_*z^!_0$, $RQ_z=z_*Rz^!_0$, and $R\Gamma_{z(B)}(P,F)=R\Gamma(B,Rz^!_0F)$, with the kernel inclusions corresponding to the closed adjunction counit. Global supported sections here mean [def-pur-support-cohomology]. In particular, for $B=\operatorname{Spec}k$ and origin $0\hookrightarrow\mathbf A^b_k$, these same normalizations give
$$R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(\mathbf A^b_k,A(r))\simeq L_{r-b}[-2b].$$

source.place: Tag 09XP (section-cohomology-support) and Tag 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic), support-kernel interpretation; current blueprint cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity proof, ordinary-etale ordered Cartier orientation and finite-level comparison. proof.text: Write $B=\operatorname{Spec}R$. Then $P=\operatorname{Spec}R[v_1,\ldots,v_b]$ by [def-sbc-affine-space], and $z$ is the quotient by $(v_1,\ldots,v_b)$. Thus $z$ is closed, $P$ is finite type over $k$, and its complement is the finite union of the affine basic opens $D(v_i)$, hence quasi-compact (empty if $b=0$). Both $B$ and $P$ are separated over $k$: the diagonal of an affine $k$-scheme $\operatorname{Spec}S$ is the closed immersion defined by the surjection $S\otimes_kS\to S$. These checks put the schemes and closed immersion in the domains of the comparison theorems used below.

source.place: The affine-space projection and zero section in the first paragraph; elementary verification of the finite-type and separated domains.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-etale-injective-support-sequence] to $z$ with the finite commutative ring $A$. Its sheaf-level assertion identifies $Q_z(F)$ with $z_*z^!_0F$ and its inclusion with the counit, in the module categories themselves. The abelian support adjunction of [lem-pur-etale-supported-kernel-adjunction] also makes the exactness of closed pushforward explicit; the same exactness holds for modules since kernels and cokernels are computed on underlying abelian sheaves. For a bounded-below injective resolution $F\to I$, $Q_z(I)=z_*z^!_0(I)$ and $z^!_0(I)$ computes the ordinary closed right adjoint, by the module support-sequence assertion. Therefore $RQ_zF=z_*Rz^!_0F$. Moreover $z^!_0$ carries injectives to injectives: an extension across a monomorphism on $B$ is equivalent by its adjunction to an extension across its exact $z_*$-image. Consequently the equality $\Gamma_{z(B)}(P,I)=\Gamma(B,z^!_0I)$ computes both derived functors, giving $R\Gamma_{z(B)}(P,F)=R\Gamma(B,Rz^!_0F)$. These module-sheaf derived functors are the abelian ones of [def-pur-support-cohomology]. By [det-pbc-conventions-module-cohomology] the underlying abelian sheaf of an injective module sheaf $I$ has no higher cohomology on $P$, on $U=P\setminus z(B)$ or on $B$. As $z_*$ has the exact left adjoint $z^{-1}$, $z_*z^!_0I$ is again injective, so the support sequence of [lem-pur-etale-injective-support-sequence] stays exact on global sections: $I(P)\to I(U)$ is onto. The long exact sequence of [thm-pur-with-support-exactness] for the underlying torsion sheaf of $I$ then gives $H^q_{z(B)}(P,I)=0$ for $q>0$. Hence module injective resolutions compute the abelian $R\Gamma_{z(B)}(P,-)$ and $R\Gamma(B,-)$. All the maps are induced by the original kernel inclusion, so their counits agree.

source.place: Tags 09XP (section-cohomology-support), 09XQ (lemma-sections-with-support-acyclic); module version of the same injective-resolution argument.

proof.text:
Put $D=Rz^!_0(A_P(b))[2b]$. This is bounded below. The finite Tate-site descent [lem-amb-finite-tate-site-descent] identifies $
u_P^*A_P(b)$ with the specified finite pro-etale twist, for every $n\geq1$. The counit-preserving comparison [lem-pur-closed-finite-adjoint-counit-transport] identifies $
u_B^*D$ with $Rz^!A_P^{\mathrm{pro}}(b)[2b]$. Now apply the already existing normalized zero-section theorem [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity] with $c=b$: it supplies an isomorphism $A_B^{\mathrm{pro}}	o
u_B^*D$. Full faithfulness of $
u_B^*$ on $D^+$ in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison] gives a unique lift $	heta_b:A_B	o D$. Lift its inverse as well; faithfulness makes both composites identities. Thus $	heta_b$ is an ordinary etale isomorphism, and Step 2 gives $RQ_zA_P(b)\cong z_*A_B[-2b]$. This is descent of an existing theorem, not a new purity hypothesis for the support kernel.

source.place: The normalized zero-section isomorphism and finite etale-origin comparison; Stacks proetale.tex Tag 09B1 (lemma-compare-derived) supplies bounded-below full faithfulness.

proof.text: The counit transpose of $\theta_b$ is the ordinary supported class $c_b:z_*A_B\to A_P(b)[2b]$. Indeed, [lem-pur-closed-finite-adjoint-counit-transport] identifies its image with the transpose of the pro-etale zero-section orientation. The normalization clause of [cor-pur-affine-space-zero-section-purity] says this transpose is the ordered product of the $b$ coordinate Cartier-Kummer classes, or the unit for $b=0$. Each factor is the image of its ordinary etale witness by [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map]; that statement includes arbitrary $n$ and independence of the annihilating exponent. The comparison of supported cup operations in [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] identifies the image of the ordinary ordered product with that pro-etale product. Faithfulness in [thm-weil-pbc-site-comparison], now on $P$, makes these actual etale morphisms equal. Thus $\theta_b(1)=\partial\kappa(v_1)\cup\cdots\cup\partial\kappa(v_b)$ with the prescribed boundary sign, including the empty product. In particular the inverse isomorphism of Step 3 has precisely the requested generator normalization.

source.place: Rank-one Cartier normalization, ordered iteration, and the exact monoidal finite site comparison.

proof.text: For $r\in\mathbf Z$ put $L=L_{r-b}=A_k(r-b)(k)$. By [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback], the twists on $P$ and $B$ are pulled back from $k$, are invertible lines, and their tensor/evaluation comparisons include negative powers. Since $k$ is algebraically closed, its roots of unity are constant: $\mu_{\ell^N,k}$ is the constant cyclic group of order $\ell^N$. Thus $L$ is free of rank one over $A$ and $A_P(r)=A_P(b)\otimes_A\underline L$. Tensor with $\underline L$ is an exact autoequivalence, with inverse tensor with $\underline{L^\vee}$, so it preserves injectives. On sheaves, the natural comparison $Q_z(F)\otimes_A\underline L\to Q_z(F\otimes_A\underline L)$ is an isomorphism: after choosing any generator of $L$ it is the identity on the defining restriction kernels. Applying this to injective resolutions proves the same comparison for $RQ_z$. Also $z_*G\otimes_A\underline L=z_*(G\otimes_A\underline L)$. Tensor the isomorphism in Step 3 with $L$ to obtain $RQ_zA_P(r)\cong z_*A_B(r-b)[-2b]$. Changing a generator of $L$ multiplies both sides by the same unit of $A$; all the maps are $A$-linear, so the comparison and orientation are independent of that choice. The tensor and evaluation identifications in the cited twist lemma show that this construction respects $A(r)=A(b)\otimes_AA(r-b)$ for all integers $r$.

source.place: The sentence that twists and shifts add; explicit constant-line tensor argument for the ordinary support kernel.

proof.text: Let $g:B'\to B$ be any morphism between the affine finite-type bases, and let $h:P'\to P$ be its affine-space base change. The coordinate divisors remain Cartier, since multiplication by each $v_i$ is injective in a polynomial ring over any base ring. By [lem-amb-cartier-kummer-map] their ordinary supported morphisms pull back to those for $P'$, independently of $N$. By [lem-pur-supported-cup-functoriality] their ordered product pulls back to $c_b'$; for $b=0$ the unit does also. The support-Hom naturality statement [lem-asd-supported-kummer-support-hom-naturality] identifies this pullback with $h^{-1}c_b$ precomposed by the inverse of the canonical isomorphism $h^{-1}z_*A_B\cong z'_*A_{B'}$. By the closed adjunction of Step 2, the canonical supported pullback $h^{-1}RQ_zA_P(b)\to RQ_{z'}A_{P'}(b)$ therefore carries the isomorphism induced by $\theta_b$ to the one induced by $\theta_b'$. This proves the required commuting square and invertibility for that specified pullback, rather than just existence of some comparison. For $r\ne b$, tensor this square with the constant line $L_{r-b}$; the pullback, tensor and exponent compatibilities in [lem-asd-etale-finite-twist-pullback] give the same square for $r$. This also proves independence of $N$ for every twist: two annihilating powers compare through their maximum, and all the factors and line identifications agree under those transition maps.

source.place: Final base-change paragraph, with the ordinary supported-Hom pullback spelled out.

proof.text: Finally take $B=\operatorname{Spec}k$. The equivalence in [lem-exc-abelian-sheaves-gmodules] has trivial Galois group because $k$ is algebraically closed. It identifies global sections with evaluation in abelian groups. Transporting the $A$-action along the same equivalence gives the equivalence with $A$-modules, so global sections on this point are exact and evaluate the constant line $A_k(r-b)$ to $L_{r-b}$. Apply derived global sections to the isomorphism of Step 5 and use the support/global identity of Step 2. This gives $R\Gamma_{\{0\}}(\mathbf A^b_k,A(r))\cong L_{r-b}[-2b]$. Since it is obtained from the same $\theta_b$ by tensor and evaluation, it has the same Kummer product normalization, not a separately chosen scalar.
